**Noise.** Per-seed SD is about 0.3 pp, so the SE of a 3-seed mean is about 0.17 pp. Time reproduces to ±0.03 s within a build. Across builds it varies by 1–2% (E059: same recipe 5.19 vs 5.08 forecast). σ_build is small (E057), so 40–60-draw comparisons resolve about 0.08–0.1 pp.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ(steps × per-step cost).
- Per-step cost: 32 px 32 ms, 28 px 26 ms, 24 px 21 ms, 20 px 16 ms.
- A stem-frozen step saves about 8.7 ms; also freezing group 2 saves about 10 ms more.
- Optimizer overhead is real. E062 removed Muon and saved 0.28 s, against 0.18 s of NS compute, so about 0.1 s is per-call overhead. That is the ceiling for I107; I expect it to recover about half.
- Removals land at or under the model (E052, E056, E061, E062), so I shade cuts down by about 3%.
- Changes that leave time unchanged land at about tip ±1.5% from the build.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost).** The dial is about 0.8 s/pp. ReLU is worse (about 0.46 s/pp), as is SGD (catastrophic). Width and selection trade at about the dial. Earlier freezes cost accuracy (E037/E053/E055). The first 12 early trims were near-free (E061). The second dose crashed (E063), probably an indexing bug when trimming into the epoch/resolution table, so it is still untested.

**Mechanisms.**
1. Accuracy is bought with optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Truncation is free only after a layer has finished learning (E041/E045/E053/E054/E055 vs E028/E060/E061).
2. Muon carries the per-step quality: SGD lost 3 pp (E062). Muon's hyperparameters were never tuned. lr ×1.5 read +0.09 pp at 3 seeds (E014). That prior is weakly positive and small. Raising momentum to 0.8 at batch 2000 is a coin flip, leaning slightly negative.
3. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is tuned (E025/E030). The LR floor does not matter under averaging (E009), so the anneal shape near the freeze should matter little (I104 is expected to be about neutral).
4. Filter wd is inert because Muon renormalizes the filters. The BN scale is frozen.
5. GELU cost is partly erf compute. tanh-GELU and SiLU may recover a third to half of ReLU's 4.8% saving. tanh-GELU stays close to exact GELU in accuracy; SiLU less so.
6. Fitting state is unknown (I109). LS 0.3 plus 225 steps likely leaves clean train top-1 around 85–92%, which means mild under-fitting.

**Lessons.** I under-forecast time savings from removals (E052, E056, E062) and over-forecast the time-neutral E059. Widen time ranges by build spread. Optimizer-core swaps need very wide accuracy ranges. Diagnostic runs report the tip's numbers.

W3 (cost lens), after E063 (crash).

**Tip (E061, 376f231).** 225 steps at batch 2000. Phases at 20/24/28/32 px run for about 59/24/71/71 steps. The whitening bias is detached at about 6%. The stem is frozen in the last 25% of steps and group 2 in the last 10%. Measured: 5.02 s and 0.7534 on seeds 0–2. The population mean is about 0.752–0.7525, so the local bar of 0.753 sits about 0.1 pp above it. Any change that costs accuracy has well under a coin-flip chance of passing locally. Any change that leaves accuracy unchanged passes about half the time.

**Noise.** Per-seed SD is about 0.3 pp, so the SE of a 3-seed mean is about 0.17 pp. Time reproduces to ±0.03 s within a build. Across builds it varies by 1–2% (E059: same recipe 5.19 vs 5.08 forecast). σ_build is small (E057), so 40–60-draw comparisons resolve about 0.08–0.1 pp.

**Time model.** Time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ(steps × per-step cost).
- Per-step cost: 32 px 32 ms, 28 px 26 ms, 24 px 21 ms, 20 px 16 ms.
- A stem-frozen step saves about 8.7 ms; also freezing group 2 saves about 10 ms more.
- Optimizer overhead is real. E062 removed Muon and saved 0.28 s, against 0.18 s of NS compute, so about 0.1 s is per-call overhead. That is the ceiling for I107; I expect it to recover about half.
- Removals land at or under the model (E052, E056, E061, E062), so I shade cuts down by about 3%.
- Changes that leave time unchanged land at about tip ±1.5% from the build.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost).** The dial is about 0.8 s/pp. ReLU is worse (about 0.46 s/pp), as is SGD (catastrophic). Width and selection trade at about the dial. Earlier freezes cost accuracy (E037/E053/E055). The first 12 early trims were near-free (E061). The second dose crashed (E063), probably an indexing bug when trimming into the epoch/resolution table, so it is still untested.

**Mechanisms.**
1. Accuracy is bought with optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Truncation is free only after a layer has finished learning (E041/E045/E053/E054/E055 vs E028/E060/E061).
2. Muon carries the per-step quality: SGD lost 3 pp (E062). Muon's hyperparameters were never tuned. lr ×1.5 read +0.09 pp at 3 seeds (E014). That prior is weakly positive and small. Raising momentum to 0.8 at batch 2000 is a coin flip, leaning slightly negative.
3. Lookahead is worth about 1 pp and is tuned (E025/E030). The LR floor does not matter under averaging (E009), so the anneal shape near the freeze should matter little (I104 is expected to be about neutral).
4. Filter wd is inert because Muon renormalizes the filters. The BN scale is frozen.
5. GELU cost is partly erf compute. tanh-GELU and SiLU may recover a third to half of ReLU's 4.8% saving. tanh-GELU stays close to exact GELU in accuracy; SiLU less so.
6. Fitting state is unknown (I109). LS 0.3 plus 225 steps likely leaves clean train top-1 around 85–92%, which means mild under-fitting.

**Lessons.** I under-forecast time savings from removals (E052, E056, E062) and over-forecast the time-neutral E059. Widen time ranges by build spread. Optimizer-core swaps need very wide accuracy ranges. Diagnostic runs report the tip's numbers.

**Unsure.** Batch elasticity under Muon; Inductor's lowering of tanh-GELU; PCIe judge drift; whether the early-trim curve stays flat beyond 225 steps (E063 crashed); the size of the Muon lr optimum.

forecasts.reason: tanh-GELU probably saves 1–2.5% (part of ReLU's 4.8%), near the 1.5% gate. If committed, accuracy is about flat but not resolvable by a 3-seed read.
Anneal-only change at equal time. Under Lookahead (E009) the LR floor matters little, so the expected effect is ≤0.1 pp, which is noise.
+0.09 s for about +0.05–0.1 pp. That is about the dial's rate, so it is unlikely to clear the ≥0.12 pp bar with confidence.
E014 read +0.09 pp. At the higher lr, renormalized filters take bigger rotations; the expected gain is about +0.05 pp, under the 0.12 pp bar.
E062 implies about 0.1 s of Muon call overhead. Batching the calls should recover about 0.04–0.07 s with identical math.
Momentum 0.8 at batch 2000 with Lookahead is a coin flip, leaning slightly harmful. A ±0.12 pp outcome is unlikely either way.
Diagnostic that reports the tip's numbers. Clean train top-1 is likely about 86–92%, which is consistent with under-fitting.

cruxes: Why did E063 crash, and once fixed, is the second 12-step early trim (225→213) still near-free (≤0.1 pp for about 0.15 s)? This decides whether early trims keep paying better than the dial.
Does tanh-GELU (or SiLU) recover at least 1.5% of step time under Inductor while staying within 0.1 pp of exact GELU? Equivalently: is GELU's cost erf compute or bytes moved?
How much of E062's unexplained 0.1 s of Muon overhead does a batched single-call Muon recover? This is the last identical-math time lever larger than build noise.
